summary: Steel lookout built by the Plymouth CCC camp in 1940; discontinued by 1954, later kept inactive; new white oak stairs went in during 2025.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower with a cab; a cabin and latrine were built on the mountain in 1940
facts.agency: Norwich Town Conservation Commission (maintains the tower)

access.note: Open hiking trail in the Woody Adams Conservation Forest; the trailhead is a small lot on Turnpike Road.

visit.trail_note: Gile Mountain Trail, a foot route with granite steps from the Turnpike Road lot to the tower.

events.note: Plymouth CCC camp built a steel lookout tower, cabin and latrine (state report, year ending June 30, 1940)
Discontinued in the 1953-54 biennium; could be put back in service if needed
Kept on an inactive basis in 1957-58, with plane patrols covering the area in hazardous weather
New white oak stairs and treads installed; volunteers, with a Norwich Women's Club grant

corrections.why: The Eastern U.S. Lookouts page gives Windsor County; Windson looks like a typo, repeated in the FFLA list.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: State reports first call the tower discontinued in 1953-54, then describe it as kept on an inactive basis in 1957-58. The FFLA lists it as standing with its cab in place.

sources.title: Vermont fire tower updates, 2025 chapter report

notes_for_editor: Record county Windson is a typo for Windsor; the FFLA list repeats it. Record height_m 20.4 (OpenStreetMap) is consistent with the approximately 70-foot figure from Norwich Trails, so it is not added as a fact. The 1940 date comes from a transcription of the state report on Eastern U.S. Lookouts, not the original. Current access and climbing rules were not confirmed with the Norwich Town Conservation Commission. The Norwich Historical Society article behind the WWII use was not read.
